subject: Operational Runway and Escalation Protocol for Observability Delivery
messages:
From: Danielle Fox <d.fox@blueharbor.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops-team@blueharbor.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Observability onboarding kickoff — scope & constraints

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the intro call earlier this week. BlueHarbor is ready to start the observability onboarding for our production inference surface. To be explicit on our priorities: dashboards for request/latency/cost, tracing hooks for cross-service flows, an error taxonomy for model responses (e.g., rate-limit vs model-failure vs malformed-input), and alert routing that maps to our oncall rotations. We also need a runbook with clear escalation steps and SLAs for pager-worthy incidents.

Attached is a short inventory (initial_requirements.xlsx) showing services, log buckets, and owners. Key constraints: we are on GCP (us-west1), have strict data-retention rules (30 days aggregated, 90 days audit), and our security team requires read-only service accounts scoped to specific projects.

Short asks to kick off implementation planning:
- Can Redwood provide a recommended dashboard layout and a small sample dashboard we can iterate on?
- Who will own the alert routing work on Redwood’s side (config + PagerDuty mapping)?
- Proposed cadence for implementation sprints (we're aiming for a two-week sprint cadence with a go-live in ~4 weeks).

We can set a standing weekly 30-minute sync if that helps.

Thanks,
Danielle
Danielle Fox
Head of Platform Ops, BlueHarbor Systems

Attachment: initial_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet - inventory of services and log locations)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Danielle Fox <d.fox@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability onboarding kickoff — scope & constraints

Hi Danielle — appreciate the clear inventory and constraints. We’re aligned on the scope and I sketched a pragmatic implementation runway to meet your 4-week target. High-level plan below; I attached an initial draft runbook (obs_runway_v0.md) for internal review.

Implementation runway (weeks):
- Week 0 (this week): Access and alignment — read-only SA, log buckets, and sample traces; identify service owners on your side.
- Week 1: Dashboards — we’ll deliver a baseline dashboard template (latency / p99 / cost per request / error rates) and a dashboard_layout_v1.png mock for sign-off.
- Week 2: Tracing hooks & error taxonomy — instrument key RPCs, add tag conventions, and propose an error taxonomy document.
- Week 3: Alert routing & runbooks — map alerts to your PagerDuty rotations, define severity classification, and finalize the runbook (oncall matrix).

Ownership (Redwood):
- Dashboard templates & layout: Laura Bennett (dashboards, owner)
- Tracing guidance & tag conventions: Ben Carter (tracing lead)
- Runbook and escalation protocol: Marissa Cole (runbooks + playbook owner)

Action items for BlueHarbor:
- Provide the read-only service account and roles by EOD Monday (email the keyholder to me directly).
- Confirm oncall rotations and PagerDuty integration contact.
- Approve weekly 30-minute sync (proposed Mondays at 10am PT).

If this looks good I’ll create the Jira ticket and attach the initial runbook draft. For visibility I opened a placeholder ticket OPS-4789 (will link in the shared Drive).

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: obs_runway_v0.md (markdown - draft runbook & timeline)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability onboarding kickoff — scope & constraints

Quick internal note before I reply to BlueHarbor:
- I’ll own the initial Grafana dashboard templates and can hand over a JSON export. Ben, can you confirm the tracing tag set (service, env, request_id, model_id, seq_len) and whether we should include kv-cache hit metrics?
- Ben, if you can draft the taxonomy matrix (category, symptom, likely_root, suggested_alert, severity) I’ll fold it into the dashboard annotations.
- Marissa, for runbooks: I recommend a 3-tier severity (SEV1: service down / model unavailable; SEV2: degraded latency or high error-rate; SEV3: noisy / infrequent faults). I’ll add dashboard alert thresholds to the OPS-4789 ticket.

Ben — if you’re okay, I’ll schedule a 30-minute working session on Wednesday to pair on tags and sample traces.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Product Reliability, Redwood Inference

Hi Danielle — looping back with confirmed owners and next steps.

What we’ve done / attachments:
- Uploaded a baseline dashboard JSON and a visual mock (dashboard_layout_v1.png) to the shared Drive.
- Draft runbook (obs_runway_v0.md) now includes the oncall matrix (runbook_oncall_matrix.csv) and a preliminary error taxonomy.
- Jira: OPS-4789 created for tracking (https://jira.redwoodai.com/browse/OPS-4789).

Confirmed Redwood owners:
- Dashboards: Laura Bennett
- Tracing & tags: Ben Carter
- Runbook & escalation flow: Marissa Cole

Proposed go-live: 2026-12-10 (subject to BlueHarbor sign-off after week-3 smoke tests).

Next steps for BlueHarbor (please):
1) Share the read-only SA by EOD Monday so we can run scoped queries and import logs.
2) Confirm PagerDuty integration contact and rotation schedules.
3) Approve the Monday 10am PT weekly sync (we’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm).

If you’d like a short working session to walk the dashboard and runbook we can do a 45-minute handoff next Tuesday.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Cheers,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
